subject: Performance acceptance & ops-run test window for private VPC inference
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <s.khan@virturehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance acceptance & ops-run test window for private VPC inference

Hi Samira — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on performance and the private VPC deployment: 

1) Target SLOs you asked us to validate during the POC:
   - Tail latency (99th): <= 200 ms for streaming token delivery under normal load
   - Sustained throughput: 500 reqs/sec for short text-generation (avg 128 tokens)
   - Concurrency: support 150 concurrent active sessions without degradation
   - Streaming requirements: initial first-byte < 120 ms, per-token stream window <= 50 ms for real-time UX
   - Egress bandwidth: reserve >= 200 Mbps for inference egress during peak windows

2) Network path constraints you raised:
   - Site-to-site VPN vs direct peering decision (you prefer peering if possible)
   - Max one-way added latency budget for our runtime: <= 25 ms
   - Packet loss tolerance: < 0.1% for stable streaming
   - MTU / fragmentation concerns on your edge NATs (we asked for traceroute and MTU info)

3) Acceptance criteria for the run:
   - Successful sustain of 80% of throughput target for 30 minutes with 99th latency <= target
   - No more than two stream disconnects per 10k sessions during the test window

Next steps / ask list (action owners in parens):
   - Send us a proposed 2-hour test window next week with preferred timezones (Samira / Infra Ops)
   - Share traceroutes, MTU, and VPN/peering contact info (Infra Ops)
   - We will deliver the perf-test-plan.xlsx and a short mutual-action-plan.md with responsibilities and rollback criteria (Hannah / Karthik)

Attachments: perf-test-plan.xlsx (load shapes + synthetic corpus), mutual-action-plan.md (test success/failure criteria).

If you confirm a window I’ll loop in our infra engineer for the run and provide ephemeral credentials and test harness notes.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <s.khan@virturehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Infra Ops <infra@virturehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance & ops-run test window for private VPC inference

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before locking a window: 

- We prefer direct peering (if Redwood can support that) but can fall back to site-to-site VPN for the first run. Who from your team manages peering setup?
- For MTU: our edge NAT currently has MTU 1500, and we’ve seen fragmentation issues on some tunnels in the past; I will attach a recent traceroute and MTU dump.
- Can your test harness simulate our streaming client behaviour (small, frequent token commits rather than large batches)? That’s critical for UX evaluation.

Available windows next week (PST): Tue 2026-05-25 08:00–11:00, Thu 2026-05-27 14:00–17:00. We can block Tue morning if you confirm resources.

Samira Khan
Head of Product, Virture Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <s.khan@virturehealth.com>, Infra Ops <infra@virturehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance & ops-run test window for private VPC inference

Thanks — quick technical plan and what we need from Virture to make the run meaningful: 

Technical approach (high level):
- Two-phase test: (A) baseline egress/latency probe (iperf3 + traceroutes) to validate path, MTU and loss; (B) load-driven streaming run using our synthetic client that mimics your small-token streaming behavior (configurable per-token commit frequency).
- We’ll run three load ramps to 50%, 80%, then 100% of your throughput target (500 reqs/sec). Each plateau holds for 10 minutes; the 80% plateau must hold for 30 minutes as acceptance.
- We will capture per-request latencies, per-token stream latencies (first-byte, per-token), packet loss, retransmit counts, and broken-stream counts.

What we need from you (deliverables):
- Traceroute and MTU dump files (Infra Ops) — attach to the shared Drive link or reply to this thread.
- An inbound IP range we should expect traffic from (to allow firewall/peering config).
- Confirmation whether you want us to use a routed peering setup or stand up a site-to-site IPSEC tunnel for the first test.

Artifacts we’ll provide before the run:
- perf-test-plan.xlsx (load profiles + exact metrics we’ll collect) — attached
- mutual-action-plan.md (cutover action matrix + rollback) — attached
- ephemeral test credentials and a short runbook (posted to Drive once window is locked)

Notes on failure modes and guardrails: if we see sustained packet loss > 0.2% or 99th latency > 350 ms during the ramp, the run will auto-fail and we will pause for triage. We’ll also stream live logs to your infra Slack channel if you provide the webhook.

I’ll start prepping the harness and can join Tue morning if that window works.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <s.khan@virturehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Infra Ops <infra@virturehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance & ops-run test window for private VPC inference

Samira — Tue 2026-05-25 08:00–10:00 PST is confirmed on our side. Action owners:
  - Virture Infra: reply with traceroutes + MTU dump and open firewall for Redwood egress IPs (Infra Ops)
  - Redwood Solutions: provision test harness, ephemeral creds, and Slack webhook (Karthik)
  - Redwood Sales: coordinate roll & success email and next steps (Hannah)

I’ve attached the perf-test-plan.xlsx and mutual-action-plan.md. Ben, can you please run the baseline probes at 07:45 PST and post traceroutes in the Drive folder? (Ben: ack)

If the baseline looks good we’ll start the 3-ramp run at 08:00 and aim to have a 30-minute hold at 80% starting ~08:20. If we meet acceptance we’ll capture a short exec summary and next steps toward Dedicated capacity or peering setup.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the run.

Hannah
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: perf-test-plan.xlsx (load shapes), mutual-action-plan.md (acceptance + rollback), traceroute-sample.txt (sample traceroute provided by Virture)
